study.question: Does withholding the additive task-feedback compressed branch from the click readout, while retaining auxiliary readouts and shared-context learning, recover click quality and outperform both the incumbent and a matched-history source? Compare source x primary readout, rather than repeating a context-only gradient intervention.
study.hypothesis: Observation: incumbent g0-r0069-buy_summary_direction click AUC0.6685318110053072; r0080 feedback allowed0.6662753801403174 versus blocked0.6664267605493608, while matched-source allowed0.667807490780828 versus blocked0.6677916086842245. Feedback allowed improves auxiliary AUCs to cart0.8283756514/fav0.8485585231/buy0.8476853559 from incumbent0.8038644311/0.8145723487/0.8280781402. Blocking only new auxiliary context inputs did not restore incumbent quality. Provisional mechanism: new branch participation in the primary forward representation and primary learning may account for much of the loss, while auxiliary-only feedback compression may improve the shared context through a different prediction task. Existing results do not isolate this primary participation. The next test removes only the additive click readout (and its loss VJP), retaining all auxiliary paths. This is a coordinated forward/primary-backward intervention, not a pure forward attribution.

study.proposed_difference: A 2x2 factorial: extension_source={task_aligned,match_duplicate} crossed with primary_extension_readout={False,True}. Every auxiliary head always retains the branch and auxiliary context gradients remain enabled. Compute every extension correction in every cell, then zero only the click correction when disabled in both train/eval. No extra learned state/RNG/loss; equal registered capacity, intentionally different active primary capacity and loss gradients. Common coefficient support/norm does not imply equal realized summary/gradient norms. All-task cells are source-equivalent controls for archived allowed r0080 executions, subject to host parity checks.
predictions: Primary-readout hypothesis predicts AUC(feedback_aux_only)>AUC(feedback_all_tasks). Compare the analogous match difference and interaction [feedback_aux_only-feedback_all_tasks]-[match_aux_only-match_all_tasks]. A positive interaction supports source-dependent primary participation at this seed, not a pure forward mechanism.

Useful auxiliary-feedback complementarity additionally requires feedback_aux_only to exceed match_aux_only and incumbent0.6685318110053072, hence both frozen sources0.660646940486458/0.660163362657485, with measured capacity/runtime disclosed. Auxiliary AUC improvement alone cannot select a winner.

At common inherited state, disabled click predictions equal incumbent predictions; auxiliary predictions/isolated gradients equal the corresponding all-task cell. All-task controls reproduce source common-state gradients and expected deterministic AUCs0.6662753801403174/0.667807490780828 if host execution is unchanged. Replays verify reproducibility only.

Feedback auxiliary improvements may persist because auxiliary branches remain present, but their absolute metrics can change as primary learning and shared context evolve. A source-by-routing interaction is exploratory until independent permitted repetition.
falsifiers: No positive feedback aux-only versus all-task click contrast rejects recovery via the tested primary-routing change; it does not refute all task-conditioned compression.

Recovery without beating incumbent and matched auxiliary-only source fails useful complementary-feedback criterion. Equal improvements in both sources suggest generic removal of harmful primary capacity rather than feedback-specific benefit.

Any all-task parity failure, label-order dependence, invalid-padding dependence, unmasked or current-label input, ownership violation or nonfinite gradients invalidates predictive interpretation until fixed through authorized host diagnostics.

A benefit explained by measured cost/capacity differences, dense clipping or adaptive single-seed selection does not establish a transfer mechanism or efficiency. Missing mediator telemetry leaves attribution unresolved.
alternative_explanations: Direct primary branch overfitting/representation scaling, changed primary item/context/query gradients and later scorer learning all change together; this suite cannot separate forward versus primary-backward causes.
Common support uses heterogeneous feedback and target matches; support availability itself is predictive. Coefficient norms are matched but summary norms and branch Jacobians are not.

Auxiliary branch shares per-task context-query parameters with the inherited branch; later auxiliary query/tower updates change shared-context gradients indirectly, even with unchanged immediate auxiliary gradients at common state.

Global dense-only clip10 couples tasks. Removing primary extension gradients can alter all dense updates. New registered capacity is matched across cells but active click capacity is deliberately smaller when disabled.

Single fixed seed, adaptive validation reuse across80 rounds, BF16 arithmetic, host runtime variability and sparse-ID frequency effects. Replaying a seed is not independent mechanism or repetition evidence.
Auxiliary label category/brand attribution and inherited official_offline delayed-feedback visibility limit production transfer. No withheld outcomes or unavailable timestamps are used.
